title: Compatibility shim, guided migrations, and automated backward-compatibility tests for deprecated behavior flags and streaming/tool-call semantics
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We are deprecating a set of behavior flags and introducing new defaults for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured-output enforcement. Many customers depend on legacy flag behavior (ordering of partial tool calls, relaxed structured output parsing, older streaming delimiters). Without a compatibility strategy we risk silent regressions in downstream apps and churn for enterprise customers requiring stable contracts.

Goal: Provide a short-term compatibility shim layer, a set of migration templates and docs, and an automated backward-compatibility test harness that runs against both hosted and dedicated deployments. The shim should allow us to accept legacy flag values and translate them to current runtime behavior, or simulate legacy outputs where safe. The effort should reduce migration burden, enable faster deprecation windows, and make rollouts measurable and reversible.
proposal_summary:
1) Implement an API compatibility shim that maps deprecated behavior flags to runtime policies. The shim will be implemented in the request ingress (control plane) so downstream runtime code can remain simplified. 2) Publish migration templates and a one-click migration checklist in Console and docs (Confluence/DevRel). 3) Build a backward-compatibility test harness that executes a canonical test matrix: streaming chunk boundaries, partial tool-call payloads, structured-output schema deviations, and error/edge cases. 4) Add monitoring (compat-flag usage, regression rate, customer breakage signals) and safe canary rollout gates.

Key deliverables: compat-shim PR, migration docs + sample client patches, test harness + nightly compatibility runs, observability dashboards and rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim exists and can be toggled per-customer via a control-plane flag
Migration template (per-language snippets + server-side config) published in docs with examples for streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs
Automated test harness runs nightly against hosted and a dedicated test cluster and reports regressions to a dashboard
Canary rollout plan documented; canary failsafe triggers automatic shim re-enable for affected customers
No new P0 regressions to structured output consumers in canary cohort over 2 weeks
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (soft launch): Ship compat-shim behind a per-customer opt-in control in the control plane; run tests against internal dogfood and 3 willing beta customers. Phase 2 (canary): Enable shim automatically for 10% of traffic on hosted API for 2 weeks with high-fidelity monitoring. Phase 3 (gradual opt-out): Communicate deprecation timeline and provide one-click migration helpers in Console; encourage customers to opt-in for upgraded behavior. Phase 4 (removal): After 90 days of 0 high-risk regressions in the cohort and migrations >80% of flagged customers, schedule deprecation removal with 30-day notice.
test_plan: Create a canonical compatibility matrix covering streaming delimiters, chunked function-call fragments, early tool exits, schema fallback for structured outputs, and legacy error codes
Implement harness tests that replay recorded customer prompt+response traces (sanitized) to detect behavior deltas
Daily regression runs against hosted and a dedicated staging pool; failures open a P0/P1 depending on impact classification
Add synthetic client fuzz tests for partial streaming and interleaved tool calls to catch edge reordering bugs
Integrate test results into the Console dashboard with per-model/per-release regression heatmaps
migration_guide_outline: Overview: Why flags are changing and what compatibility buys you
Quick start: one-click toggle in Console and command-line migration helper (curl + SDK snippet)
Per-language client patches: Node, Python, Java, Go examples for consuming new streaming boundaries and function call frames
Structured outputs: schema validation helper and fallback strategies (lenient parsing, envelope wrappers)
Tool calling: how to migrate from permissive partial-call behavior to strict call-then-args flow, example adapter code
Testing checklist: end-to-end flow to run against your app before you turn off the shim
Rollback playbook: steps to re-enable shim and collect diagnostic artifacts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shim complexity balloons and becomes a permanent compatibility layer -> Mitigation: Keep shim mapping table small and time-boxed (90 days). Schedule a follow-up decomp RFC if retention needed.
Risk: Silent regressions for low-traffic customers -> Mitigation: Add sampling + trace capture for any shim-translated request and proactively notify customers with sample diffs.
Risk: Test harness flakiness due to non-deterministic models -> Mitigation: Use deterministic seeds, model-anchored baselines and accept measured tolerance thresholds in assertions.
Risk: Performance overhead at ingress -> Mitigation: Implement shim as lightweight header-driven translator and benchmark; fall back to per-customer routing when overhead exceeds threshold.

Risk: Security implications for transforming tool-call payloads -> Mitigation: Security review of transformation rules, preserve original request payloads in logs for audit, do not mutate signatures or auth tokens
